note: The local test package is not release-certified. Statuses: pass (the aspect's stated scope is evidenced and passes; what the criterion needs beyond that scope is its own not-run aspect), fail (an observed or recorded correctness failure), blocked (cannot be exercised because of a recorded failure or an unsupported capability), not-run (no evidence yet). A criterion is fail if any aspect fails, otherwise blocked if any is blocked, otherwise not-run if any has not run, otherwise pass. Deferred certification is listed once, under deferredCertification, and is not part of any criterion's status. Built by tools/build_acceptance_index.py; MMR-1 adds the final scenario.

criteria.text: A pinned FWGC++ build and version-matched Bannerlord/Modding Kit/War Sails setup are reproducibly identified and verified; the existing stale generator binary is not accepted as installation evidence.

aspects.aspect: the producer is pinned and its build verified
aspects.note: fwg.exe 564c2629... from FWGC++ commit ec5d1c10; CTest 5/5; MMR-22 22/22 lock and process checks. tests/check_producer_lock.py re-checks the lock, the binary and the FWGC++ checkout. Whether a fresh build reproduces the pinned bytes is not shown; tools/Build-Fwg.ps1 does not check out the pinned commit.

aspects.aspect: the stale generator binary is not accepted
aspects.note: Any binary other than the pin is refused before launch (pin_mismatch), by the deploy, the package and the module itself. The stale binary in the FWGC++ tree (generator/build/apps/Release/fwg.exe) hashes 5867006c40876b4c..., not the pin (hashed by this audit, 2026-10-18).

aspects.aspect: the game and War Sails versions are identified and pinned
aspects.note: Bannerlord v1.4.8.119303 and War Sails v1.2.8.119303; 25 assemblies (18 game, 6 framework, Harmony) and 6 descriptors pinned by SHA-256; build and deploy refuse other inputs.

aspects.aspect: the Modding Kit is identified
aspects.note: Identified by its Steam depot 4456490 and manifest 1015157637537524692 and one editor session that opened and rendered the War Sails map (2026-10-13; the record is an inspection, so it says ticketAccepted false). No build or player step uses it. Not re-checked since.

aspects.aspect: generation is reproducible
aspects.note: MMR-24 75/75 identity and retry checks; MMR-23 120/120 source contract checks.

criteria.text: Bannerlord's New Campaign flow generates a fresh chosen-seed world locally with progress/cancel/error handling, without a player running an external editor, publishing a module or restarting the game.

aspects.aspect: New Procedural Campaign entry and setup screen
aspects.note: MMR-43 run 13032 19/19; 29 offline checks.

aspects.aspect: the generation job: progress, cancel and errors, in the running game
aspects.note: MMR-44 run 21316 17/17: cancel in 4 phases, a killed producer gives generate.crashed, largest frame gap 0.407 s. No external editor, module publishing or restart. (generator-probe.json is MMR-15's developer-menu run; that menu and its generation_menu probe were removed on 2026-10-18, and the setup screen covers the same flow.)

aspects.aspect: preview, regeneration and Start Campaign
aspects.note: MMR-46 run 50304 16/16; MMR-45 run 43676 15/15 (world A committed and played).

aspects.aspect: an interrupted generation is recovered
aspects.note: MMR-47 crash run 28280 and resume run 47264, 8/8.

aspects.aspect: the measured first-test profile
aspects.note: MMR-56 run 35468 20/20. The first Start Campaign blocks the engine thread about 383 s (the game does not respond); the wait text says so.

aspects.aspect: the clean package generates and starts a world
aspects.note: MMR-57 run 9276: seed 42 in 37.3 s, the map after 427.7 s, 358 settlements.

aspects.aspect: a chosen seed gives a playable world
aspects.note: Only seed 42 starts a campaign. Seed 43 exhausts its 3 quality attempts (generate.exhausted); seeds 44-72 were refused by the quality gate on an earlier build and not re-tried; seed 73 generates and is offered with Start Campaign, but its activation is refused at the village binding (s4). docs/research/map-epic-2-findings.md estimates a random seed fails all 3 attempts about 90 % of the time. The refusals are clean, but the player cannot generally choose a seed and play it.

criteria.text: The entire generated globe is playable as a flat map with connected east/west edges. Terrain, player/AI land and naval routes, distances, encounters, camera/picking and saves use one consistent periodic topology; different seeds change geography and traversability.

aspects.aspect: periodic coordinates and distances
aspects.note: MMR-64 run 6292 16/16; 82 offline checks on world A. East-west distances overstate sphere distance by 1/cos(latitude) (docs/periodic-coordinates.md).

aspects.aspect: generated terrain renders and answers heights, rays and picking
aspects.note: MMR-16 run 32896; MMR-37 32/32. Exact native bin-boundary rounding is unresolved (docs/runtime-backend-decision.md R02).

aspects.aspect: land and naval routes agree with the engine on generated worlds
aspects.note: MMR-38 run 42984: world A 826/826 routes, world B 1118/1118; MMR-41 21/21 with navigation caches cold, reused and faulted.

aspects.aspect: travel, camera and picking across the seam, on the periodic fixture; travel across it on world A
aspects.note: MMR-63/65/66 ran on the 4-settlement periodic fixture (mnbl_00063042). On world A, MMR-49 run 48048 crossed the seam, was pursued across it and called a fleet across it, and all of it survived save and load.

aspects.aspect: camera and picking across the seam on a generated world; mouse dragging across it; encyclopedia map navigation
aspects.note: Implemented; observed only on the fixture (camera, picking) or not at all (dragging, encyclopedia).

aspects.aspect: different seeds change geography and traversability
aspects.note: Worlds A (seed 42) and B (seed 73) differ in every geography hash (36.8 % of cells share a class) and in their engine routes (826 vs 1118). B is not playable (s4), so the difference is shown on compiled worlds and engine routes, not in play.

aspects.aspect: encounters and missions at the seam
aspects.note: One land mission at the seam ran (MMR-42 run 17596). A naval encounter, a siege, a raid, embarking and disembarking at the seam were not run in game (docs/runtime-backend-decision.md, docs/mission-scenes.md).

aspects.aspect: one consistent topology everywhere
aspects.note: Known defects, found by review and not fixed (minor): a storm that crosses the seam can miss one hourly damage tick (water-climate-review L14); distance-sorted interface lists, menu texts and map step sounds still measure planar positions near the cut (docs/periodic-presentation.md); siege machines draw only on the settlement's own side of the cut. A route whose path leaves the terrain cannot be represented.

criteria.text: Generated towns, villages, castles, factions, clans and characters initialize a coherent Sandbox campaign with trading, recruitment, ownership, wars and missions, with no unintended Calradia campaign objects surviving.

aspects.aspect: generated factions, clans, heroes, settlements and economy register and validate

recorded.status: c1-c3 evidenced for new-game initialization plus two campaign days per world; save/load, UI-driven interactions, settlement visuals and long-run economy unproved

aspects.note: World A: 358 settlements, 40 kingdoms, 92 clans. The MMR-30/33/34/35/36 in-game probes ran on 4-settlement fixtures; the whole world is covered by MMR-45 and MMR-51. One town starts with no gold and earns it within the day; 22 of 40 kingdoms hold a single fief.

aspects.aspect: no unintended Calradia campaign objects survive
aspects.note: The graph validator refuses official objects, references and coordinates; MMR-51 run 41920 found 0 settlements, clans or kingdoms outside the world.

aspects.aspect: trading, recruitment, ownership and wars
aspects.note: MMR-51 run 41920 55/55, 14 scenarios, 1 day 6 h on world A and 12 h on the fixture world. Trade and recruitment drive the screens' logic without the screens. Long play is deferred certification.

aspects.aspect: land missions and mission transitions
the remaining land missions
aspects.note: Not opened: village raids, lord's hall fights, port visits. Not played through: a wetland battle (neither world has wetland), a field battle fought to the end (all ended by retreat), the hideout's night stealth mission; siege preparation was watched for 1.5 h only; captivity escape was applied instantly.

aspects.aspect: every generated world initializes
aspects.note: Seed 73 generates and previews, but its campaign is refused at activation: the village binding leaves towns with 6-8 villages and towns and castles with none. Recorded in reviewed evidence; no run artifact of the refused start is in the repository.

criteria.text: War Sails ports, fleets, embarkation, land/sea routes, navigation types and required distance caches operate on the generated world; naval travel and naval encounters are tested.

aspects.aspect: ports, fleets and naval faction records
aspects.note: MMR-35: 15 offline checks; in-game run 21180 on the fixture world.

aspects.aspect: naval navigation types, routes and distance caches
aspects.note: Naval routes agree with the engine on world A; the Naval caches and drop-off ports are built and reused.

aspects.aspect: water, flow and weather on the generated world
aspects.note: MMR-59 23/23; MMR-39 runs on fixtures. Rivers have no water surface; 15 of 23 lake groups on world A have no plane.

aspects.aspect: naval travel, embarkation and encounters on world A
aspects.note: MMR-53 run 46036 104/104: shipyard, port and island voyages, drop-off, coastal landing, blockade, pirate battle (retreat), seaborne raid, defeat with the raft; AI 54 port and 36 island arrivals. A naval encounter at the seam is s3's.

aspects.aspect: naval combat and the rest of War Sails play
aspects.note: Not exercised: boarding, crew reinforcement, ship damage in battle, a naval battle won by fighting, a blockade battle or an AI blockade, straits narrower than 8.5, pirate-initiated encounters (the player was ignored), port visits.

aspects.aspect: fleets survive save and load
aspects.note: Embarked and post-battle fleets survive save and load (MMR-49).

criteria.text: Two campaigns with different world identities can be saved, alternately loaded after a cold restart, and resumed with correct terrain, objects and navigation; missing or mismatched worlds fail safely before simulation.

aspects.aspect: saves bind to their world; alternate loads after a cold restart
aspects.note: MMR-49: create run 48048 37/37, cold run 39860 20/20, load check 28224 3/3; MMR-19 17/17; MMR-48 14/14. MMR-49 was not re-run after MMR-51's refactor; the MMR-57 clean-install reload is the latest load. 30 handled first-chance NullReferenceExceptions per load, source unknown, are recorded in docs/runtime-capabilities.md and not resolved.

aspects.aspect: missing or mismatched worlds are refused before simulation
aspects.note: Refusals observed in game: damaged-save, missing-world, damaged-world and incompatible-build (4: one in the two-world matrix, three in the compatibility matrix). Each left the running campaign as it was. A failure after a load has started, the deferred re-encode and War Sails absent were not run in game.

aspects.aspect: a campaign is exported and imported with its world, offline
aspects.note: tools/Transfer-WorldSave.ps1 (a repository tool, not in the package): a real export imported into an empty store on the same PC and checked by tools/Inspect-World.ps1. That run used the first export format, which docs later found could not load without its activation evidence; the current format is tested offline only.

aspects.aspect: a transferred campaign loads in the game
aspects.note: No imported save was loaded in game.

aspects.aspect: the packaged module reloads a save after a reinstall
aspects.note: MMR-57 run 40996: no scene left, the save loaded and its scene was re-encoded.

aspects.aspect: two campaigns from production-generated worlds
aspects.note: The second campaign of every two-world test is the MMR-19 fixture world (mnbl_00059042, seed 364610, no bundle), because only seed 42 activates (s2, s4). Blocked by those failures, not by an unsupported capability.

deferredCertification.note: 31 seeds were tried on an earlier build (1 published) and seeds 42, 43 and 73 on the current one. Size 129 only.
No sweep of generated worlds through the game exists.
The longest play is 1 day 6 h on world A (MMR-51). Long-run economy, raids, sieges and naval attrition over many days are untested.
One working-set measurement per phase in one profile run.
The weather model was checked against its formula for all four seasons on fixtures; no season-long play.
One machine (Core Ultra 9, RTX 5080, 32 GB) at a 60 fps cap; narrow screens and UI scales measured, not run; no mission frame rate.
The budget is provisional and not enforced. The first start of every world, and the first start or load after a module update, blocks the engine thread for about 6.4 minutes.
